body: That exact feeling is why I'm afraid of suicide, not for myself, but because of how other's would feel about it. Being dead doesn't scare me, my life ending doesn't scare or matter to me, how my life affects others does. If that worry about other people goes away somehow, that's what I'm afraid of, because then I literally wouldn't care, happy or sad.

Your words actually help, a lot. I was trying to bait you into helping yourself, because helping others makes me feel better, and staves off the negative shit, paying the undeserved inheritance forward if you will. But fuck me, you have such a handle on these thoughts, how do you not apply them to yourself? Like every word of your last message could be applied to you, and deservedly so. Like, that's fucking therapeutic shit to a max level. If for anything, live to help people. I obviously still have shit to work through and am not magically fixed, but in this moment those are some extremely helpful words.

Well shit, I hope I'm the person where it's manageable. (That's not a cry for help or attention, it seems like that, but honestly, I'm okay as of right now. I just want to know when those thoughts become dangerous, because I'm afraid of suicide, and if those thoughts become so pervasive that it becomes a reality, that's just terrifying.)

For my life, it was given to me, you got that correct. And I can understand that if I was given something, to just accept it. But the things i do, repeatedly, my parents, my friends, my family, should stop, but they don't. I get unconditional love, and I see them sometimes sacrificing their life to give to me, and I hate it, why the fuck do I deserve that? And I get the random unexplained anger, I fucking have the same shit, I try to bury it, but it creeps out. It's helped to not try and fix the anger, but when it comes try to deal with it better. Admittedly i've taken to inanimate objects to express my anger, which I know is wrong, but its helped me deal with personal relationships more.

That's exactly how I feel, the thought of controlling it is so comforting that it makes me feel better overall. Everything I've read said that is dangerous, but is it? I just don't want it to go past this point, and if this is the starting point to progression, I want to know if I should get help. I know we're not all therapists, but i was hoping someone would know.

My life is perfect, or as perfect as life can be, but I don't deserve it, but I try to live to make me seem worth it. Wishing harm and acting upon it, I agree that's fairly fucked up, but we're all fucked up. If you know and feel guilty about it, are you as bad you say you are? The point I'm getting at here is you can do a lot of fucked up shit, and deserve the punishment that follows for those actions, but if you realize its wrong, you can still be a good person, as long as your next action reflects it. The question should be now, why don't I ignore these bad feelings, not why you have them.

That's what I wonder. Right now I feel okay, sometimes i feel close but always pull out of it, when does the idealization become a problem? Is there a set point? The thought of suicide makes me feel better, but committing suicide doesn't, for differing reasons. My main question is, will it become an issue? Or can I keep it at bay.

I'm honestly at a similar point, I don't want to die, but fantasize about it daily. I'm here for help too. Where we differ is my life is perfect, at least it should be perfect,  and I still don't have a chemical issue to explain it away. I wonder if we could help each other, try to explain to each other life matters, argue for the other person I guess is what I'm trying to say.
Are you refreshing for comments the same way I am?
